newsitem.title: GERMANY: German BHW sets issue price at 26 marks.
newsitem.headline: German BHW sets issue price at 26 marks.

text.p: Shares in German savings, finance and insurance group BHW Holdings AG will be priced at 26 marks each when they debut on the Frankfurt and Hanover bourses on Monday, the group said at the weekend.

BHW, Germany's second largest construction financing group, said that there were offers to buy 685 million shares, which means the issue volume of 47 million shares had been oversubscribed 14.5 times.

This adds up to a total flotation volume of 1.4 billion marks, including a "greenshoe" option, or over-allotment of extra shares, BHW, traditionally a favourite of Germany's civil servants, said in a statement issued on Saturday.

BHW has said previously that the flotation of around 30 percent of its capital would gain it entry into the M-DAX index of 70 medium-sized German publicly-quoted companies by the second half of this year.

The share has been on offer via a bookbuilding process at between 22 and 28 marks each in the past two weeks. Around 80 percent of the issue volume had been placed in Germany, with 20 percent going abroad, BHW said.
Sixty-five percent of the issue would go to institutional investors, with the remainder going to private investors.
"This means a fair and balanced allocation. We want to bring in a stable shareholder structure," management board chairman Reinhard Wagner said.

BHW said that of the 47 million shares on offer, 27 million shares will come from a capital raise by the company, while the remaining 20 will come from the group's two main shareholders, BGAG and BTA.
The two main shareholders have allocated a greenshoe option of 15 percent of the issue volume to the consortium banks.

German analysis firm Independent Research said earlier this month that a price set at the upper end of the bookbuilding range would put BHW on a price-earnings ratio of over 23 on current year estimated earnings.
This compares with a range of between 18 and 19 in the rest of the banking sector.
It advised investors to start taking profit on the stock once it rose above 30 marks.
The lead managers of the flotation are Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Credit Suisse First Boston. (( --Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525))
